medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily, titrate up to 10 mg daily as tolerated
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin system blockade to reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first_line_treatment: ACE inhibitor for CKD with albuminuria or hypertension

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually, continue while eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.purpose: Slows CKD progression and reduces cardiovascular risk in diabetic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first_line_treatment: SGLT2 inhibitor for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (risk‑equivalent condition)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first_line_treatment: Statin for all CKD patients

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; contraindicated in CKD stage 3b
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; NICE NG203 advises against dual RAAS blockade
contraindications.alternative: Use either an ACE‑I (Ramipril) or an ARB (Losartan), not both

contraindications.reason: Nephrotoxic and can worsen renal function in CKD
contraindications.alternative: Consider alternative mood stabiliser (e.g., valproate) with renal safety

contraindications.reason: Risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy when eGFR <30; patient eGFR 38.7 but precaution still advised
contraindications.alternative: Use low‑osmolar contrast with hydration protocol or avoid if possible

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure not recorded – assume untreated hypertension; obtain BP measurements before titrating Ramipril
Serum potassium not available – baseline K+ required before starting ACE‑I and for monitoring
Liver function tests not available – baseline ALT/AST required before initiating Atorvastatin
Quantitative urine ACR not provided – needed to confirm albuminuria level for monitoring response
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I or statin hypersensitivity before prescribing
HbA1c and current diabetes regimen not documented – needed to assess risk of hypoglycaemia with dapagliflozin
treatment_summary: Start ramipril, dapagliflozin, and atorvastatin as first‑line therapies per NICE NG203 to slow CKD progression, reduce proteinuria, and lower cardiovascular risk. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, and liver enzymes after initiation and at regular intervals. Avoid chronic NSAIDs, dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy, lithium, and unprotected IV contrast. Obtain missing baseline data (BP, K+, LFTs, ACR, HbA1c, allergy status) before finalising doses.
